questions.q:
10 distinct points are taken on a circle. Then using these points
Statement I : The number of triangles that can be formed is 100
Statement II : The number of chords that can be formed is 45
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Triangles $=\,{}^{10}C_3=120\neq100$ (Statement I false). Chords $=\,{}^{10}C_2=45$ (Statement II true).

questions.q: How many ways can you arrange all the letters and numbers in "KCET 2025" which start with K and end with 5?
questions.explanation: "KCET 2025" has 8 symbols (K,C,E,T,2,0,2,5) with the digit 2 repeated. Fixing K first and 5 last leaves 6 symbols (C,E,T,2,0,2) with one repeated pair, giving $\dfrac{6!}{2!}=360$ arrangements.

questions.q: The number of four digit even number that can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2 and 3 without repetition is
questions.explanation: Last digit 0: remaining 3 digits arranged in 3! = 6 ways; last digit 2: first digit ≠ 0 gives 2×2! = 4 ways; total 6+4 = 10.

questions.q: The number of diagonals that can be drawn in an octagon is

questions.explanation: Using ${}^nC_r+{}^nC_{r-1}={}^{n+1}C_r$ repeatedly on ${}^{45}C_3+{}^{45}C_4,{}^{46}C_3,\dots$ collapses the sum telescopically to ${}^{50}C_4$.

questions.q: Ten chairs are numbered as 1 to 10. Three women and two men wish to occupy one chair each. First the women choose the chairs marked 1 to 6, then the men choose the chairs from the remaining. The number of possible ways is
questions.explanation: Women arrange in 3 of the 6 chairs: $^6P_3$ ways; men then arrange in 2 of the remaining 4 chairs (7-10): $^4P_2$ ways. Total $=\,{}^6P_3\times{}^4P_2$.

questions.q: If all permutations of the letters of the word MASK are arranged in the order as in dictionary with or without meaning, which one of the following is 19$^{th}$ word?
questions.explanation: Alphabetical letters A, K, M, S each start 6 words (3! each): words 1-6 start with A, 7-12 with K, 13-18 with M, 19-24 with S. The 19th word is the first S-word, formed as S followed by A,K,M in order, i.e. SAKM — which is not among the printed options, so this appears to be a defective question, consistent with the KEA grace mark. Option (C) is picked as the closest. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: A student has to answer 10 questions, choosing at least 4 from each of the parts A and B. If there are 6 questions in part A and 7 in part B, then the number of ways the student can choose 10 questions is
The number of 4 digit numbers without repetition that can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 in which each number has two odd digits and two even digits is
questions.explanation: Choose 2 of the 4 odd digits ($^4C_2=6$) and 2 of the 3 even digits ($^3C_2=3$), then arrange the 4 chosen digits in $4!=24$ ways: $6\times3\times24=432$.

questions.q: Everybody in a room shakes hands with everybody else. The total number of handshakes is 45. The total number of persons in the room is
The number of ways in which 5 girls and 3 boys can be seated in a row so that no two boys are together is
questions.explanation: Arrange 5 girls in $5!$ ways creating 6 gaps; place 3 boys in gaps in $^6P_3$ ways: $120\times120=14400$.

questions.q: If ${}^nC_{12}={}^nC_8$ then n is equal to
The remainder obtained when $1!+2!+3!+\cdots+11!$ is divided by 12 is ____
questions.explanation: For $n\ge4$, $n!$ is divisible by 12, so the remainder is that of $1!+2!+3!=9$.

questions.q: How many 5 digit telephone numbers can be constructed using the digits 0 to 9, if each number starts with 67 and no digit appears more than once?
questions.explanation: The first two digits are fixed as 6,7. The remaining 3 digits are chosen from the other 8 digits without repetition: $8\times7\times6=336$.

$49^2-4=47\times51$ and $49^3-49=49\times48\times50$, so the product is $47\times51\times49\times48\times50=281887200$, which is exactly divisible by $6!=720$, $5!=120$ and $7!=5040$, but not by $9!$.
